title: THE ALTAR YOU’VE BEEN AVOIDING
paragraphs:
THE ALTAR YOU’VE BEEN AVOIDING
Why Romans 12:1 Is Not a Suggestion—It’s a Surrender That Changes Everything
There is a moment most believers never talk about out loud.

Not in church.
Not in small groups.
Not even in prayer.
It’s the quiet resistance inside you when you realise… God is not just asking for your sins.
He’s asking for you.

Not the polished version.
Not the Sunday version.
Not the “I’m trying my best” version.
All of you.
And suddenly, faith doesn’t feel comfortable anymore.
It feels like an altar.
Paul writes in Romans 12:1, but if you slow down and really listen, it doesn’t read like a gentle encouragement. It sounds like a plea that carries the weight of eternity:

“Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί…”
(Parakalō oun hymas, adelphoi…)
“I urge you therefore, brothers…”
That Greek word παρακαλῶ (parakalō) is not casual. It’s not a suggestion. It’s a deep, heartfelt appeal—a desperate urging born from love and truth.
Paul is saying, “After everything God has done… how can you not respond?”
And then he anchors it:

“διὰ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ”
(dia tōn oiktirmōn tou Theou)
“by the mercies of God…”

Not by guilt.
Not by fear.
Not by obligation.
By mercy.

The same mercy that found you when you were hiding.
The same mercy that didn’t expose you to shame, but covered you in grace.
The same mercy that saw your worst moments and still chose you.
And now… that mercy is asking for something in return.

“παραστῆσαι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν θυσίαν ζῶσαν…”
(parastēsai ta sōmata hymōn thysian zōsan)
“to present your bodies as a living sacrifice…”
A living sacrifice.
This is where it gets uncomfortable.
Because in the Old Testament, sacrifices died once… and it was over.
But a living sacrifice?
That means you keep climbing back onto the altar.
Every. Single. Day.

When your pride wants control.
When your flesh wants comfort.
When your mind wants to wander.
When your heart wants what God said no to.
You don’t just “believe” in Jesus.
You die daily to everything that competes with Him.
The Hebrew concept behind sacrifice—זֶבַח (zevach)—was never about convenience. It was costly. It was visible. It was intentional.
You didn’t accidentally become a sacrifice.
You chose it.
And Paul says this sacrifice is:

“ἁγίαν, εὐάρεστον τῷ Θεῷ”
(hagían, euáreston tō Theō)
“holy and pleasing to God…”
Holy doesn’t mean perfect.
It means set apart.

Different.
Marked.
Unavailable to the patterns that once owned you.
And pleasing… not to people.
To God.
Let that sink in.

You can fool people and still not please God.
You can impress a crowd and still resist surrender.
You can look spiritual and still be withholding your life.
But when you lay yourself down fully—your thoughts, your desires, your plans, your identity—that is what moves the heart of God.
And Paul ends with something that most people read too quickly:

“τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν ὑμῶν”
(tēn logikēn latreian hymōn)
“your reasonable service” or “your true worship.”
Reasonable.
Logical.
In other words… after everything Jesus has done for you…
this is the only response that makes sense.

Not half-hearted faith.
Not selective obedience.
Not occasional devotion.
Total surrender.
And here’s the truth that many avoid:
You cannot carry your cross and your comfort at the same time.
You cannot follow Jesus and keep negotiating the terms.
You cannot call Him Lord and still live like you belong to yourself.
This is where the scandal turns into grace.
Because the same altar that feels like death…
becomes the place where God rewrites everything.

Your shame becomes testimony.
Your weakness becomes strength.
Your past becomes a witness of redemption.
You thought surrender would cost you everything.
But what it actually does…
is give you back the life you were created to live.
Be honest.
There are areas you haven’t placed on the altar yet.

Habits you justify.
Thoughts you entertain.
Dreams you won’t release.
Wounds you refuse to surrender.
And God is not exposing you to condemn you.
He’s inviting you… to be free.
So let me ask you something that deserves an honest answer:
What are you still holding back from God?
Sit with it.
Because that one thing… might be the very thing keeping you from experiencing the fullness of His presence.
If this hit something deep inside you, don’t ignore it.
Be real. Someone else needs to see your honesty and realise they’re not alone.
And if you truly desire to glorify God… not just in words but in your life…
then support what spreads His truth.
Because staying close to truth is how you stay alive in faith.
Because the altar is not the end of your story…
…it’s where God begins rewriting it.
And one day, you will look back and realise—

the thing you were afraid to surrender
was the very thing God used to set you free.
